During the northward course [of the sun], in the bright fortnight, under an auspicious asterism, except on the ninth [tithis].

sanskrit_iast: jayaprabhṛtirhutvā 'uṣṇena vāyurudakenedyajamānasyāyuṣā savitā varuṇodadhadyajamānāya dāśuṣe' ityuṣṇā apo 'bhimantrayate |
meaning: जयप्रभृतिर्हुत्वा ऽउष्णेन वायुरुदकेनेद्यजमानस्यायुषा सविता वरुणोदधद्यजमानाय दाशुषेऽ इत्युष्णा अपो ऽभिमन्त्रयते ।
text_mt:
"With warm water, O Vāyu, come with the life of the sacrificer; / may Savitṛ and Varuṇa grant it to the sacrificer who gives gifts,"

with this he consecrates the warm water.

sanskrit_iast: aditiḥ keśānvapatvāya udantu jīvase dhārayatu prajāpatiḥ punaḥ punaḥ svastaye' || ityabhyundati |
meaning: अदितिः केशान्वपत्वाय उदन्तु जीवसे धारयतु प्रजापतिः पुनः पुनः स्वस्तयेऽ ॥ इत्यभ्युन्दति ।
text_mt: "May Aditi shave the hair; may the waters moisten it for life; / may Prajāpati preserve it again and again for well-being,"
With "O herb, protect him!" he places a darbha-blade inside near the right hairline.
With "O razor, do not harm him!" he applies the razor.

sanskrit_iast: yenāvapatsavitā kṣureṇa somasya rājño varuṇasya keśān | tena brāhmaṇo vapatvāyuṣmānayaṃ jaradaṣṭhirastu || yena pūṣā bṛhaspaterindriyasya cāyuṣe 'vapat | tena te vapāmyāyuṣe dīrdhāyutvāya jīvase || yena bhūyaścaratyayaṃ jyokca paśyati sūryaḥ | tena te vapāmyāyuṣe suślokyāya svastaye || iti tisṛbhistriḥ pravapati |
meaning: येनावपत्सविता क्षुरेण सोमस्य राज्ञो वरुणस्य केशान् । तेन ब्राह्मणो वपत्वायुष्मानयं जरदष्ठिरस्तु ॥ येन पूषा बृहस्पतेरिन्द्रियस्य चायुषे ऽवपत् । तेन ते वपाम्यायुषे दीर्धायुत्वाय जीवसे ॥ येन भूयश्चरत्ययं ज्योक्च पश्यति सूर्यः । तेन ते वपाम्यायुषे सुश्लोक्याय स्वस्तये ॥ इति तिसृभिस्त्रिः प्रवपति ।
text_mt:
"With which razor Savitṛ shaved the hair of King Soma and Varuṇa, / with that let the Brāhmaṇa shave; may he be long-lived and reach old age."

"With which Pūṣan shaved for Bṛhaspati, and for the life and vigor of Indra, / with that I shave you for life, for longevity, for living."

"By which this one walks further and long beholds the sun, / with that I shave you for life, for good renown, for well-being."

sanskrit_iast: yatkṣureṇa vartayatā sutejasā vaptarvapasi keśān | śundhi śiro māsyāyuḥ pramorṣīḥ || iti lauhāyasaṃ kṣuraṃ keśāvāpāya prayacchati |
meaning: यत्क्षुरेण वर्तयता सुतेजसा वप्तर्वपसि केशान् । शुन्धि शिरो मास्यायुः प्रमोर्षीः ॥ इति लौहायसं क्षुरं केशावापाय प्रयच्छति ।
text_mt:
With these three [verses] he shaves three times.

"When with the gliding razor of bright edge you, the barber, shave the hair, / cleanse his head; do not rob his life!"

With this he gives the copper-iron razor to the barber.

sanskrit_iast: mā te keśānanugādvarca etattathā dhātā dadhātu te | tubhyamindro varuṇo bṛhaspatiḥ savitā varcā ādadhuḥ || iti pravapato 'numantrayate |
meaning: मा ते केशाननुगाद्वर्च एतत्तथा धाता दधातु ते । तुभ्यमिन्द्रो वरुणो बृहस्पतिः सविता वर्चा आदधुः ॥ इति प्रवपतो ऽनुमन्त्रयते ।
text_mt:
"May this luster not go away following your hair; thus may Dhātṛ ordain for you! / May Indra, Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, and Savitṛ bestow luster upon you!"

With this he recites over him as he shaves.
A friend gathers the shorn hair in a lump of fresh cow dung.

sanskrit_iast: uptvāya keśānvaruṇāsya rājño bṛhaspatiḥ savitā viṣṇuragniḥ | tebhyo nidhānaṃ mahataṃ na vidannantarā dyāvāpṛthivyorapasyuḥ || iti prāgudīco hriyamāṇānanumantrayate |
meaning: उप्त्वाय केशान्वरुणास्य राज्ञो बृहस्पतिः सविता विष्णुरग्निः । तेभ्यो निधानं महतं न विदन्नन्तरा द्यावापृथिव्योरपस्युः ॥ इति प्रागुदीचो ह्रियमाणाननुमन्त्रयते ।
text_mt:
"Having shorn the hair of this King Varuṇa, Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, Viṣṇu, and Agni / did not find a great resting place for them between heaven and earth, working busily."

With this he recites over [the hairs] being carried toward the northeast.
[The child] should attach [the hair] with his wife into a non-empty [vessel]: so says the Vedic revelation.

sanskrit_iast: varaṃ kartre dadāti pakṣmaguḍaṃ tilapiślaṃ ca keśavāpāya |
meaning: वरं कर्त्रे ददाति पक्ष्मगुडं तिलपिश्लं च केशवापाय ।
text_mt: He gives a choice gift to the performer, and a lump of unrefined sugar and pounded sesame to the barber.

sanskrit_iast: etena tu kalpena ṣoḍaśe varṣe godānamagniṃ vādhyeṣyamāṇasyāgnirgodāniko maitrāyaṇiriti śrutiḥ |
meaning: एतेन तु कल्पेन षोडशे वर्षे गोदानमग्निं वाध्येष्यमाणस्याग्निर्गोदानिको मैत्रायणिरिति श्रुतिः ।
text_mt: By this procedure, however, in the sixteenth year [is performed] the gift of a cow (godāna) or for one who is going to study the fire [ritual]; 'the fire belongs to the godāna rite, a Maitrāyaṇī [text],' such is the Vedic revelation.

sanskrit_iast: aditiḥ śmaśruḥ vapatvityūdena śmaśrupravapati śundhi mukhamiti ca || ityekaviṃśaḥ khaṇḍaḥ || saptame navame vopāyanam |
meaning: अदितिः श्मश्रुः वपत्वित्यूदेन श्मश्रुप्रवपति शुन्धि मुखमिति च ॥ इत्येकविंशः खण्डः ॥ सप्तमे नवमे वोपायनम् ।
text_mt:
With the water [mantra] 'May Aditi shave the beard,' he shaves the beard, and [recites] 'Cleanse the face.'

In the seventh or in the ninth [year is] the initiation.

sanskrit_iast: āgantrā samaganmahi prathamamartiṃ yuyotu naḥ | ariṣṭāḥ saṃcaremahi svasti caratā diśaḥ | svastyāgṛhebhyaḥ || ityuptakeśena snātenāktenābhyaktenālaṃkṛtena yajñopavītinā sametya japati |
meaning: आगन्त्रा समगन्महि प्रथममर्तिं युयोतु नः । अरिष्टाः संचरेमहि स्वस्ति चरता दिशः । स्वस्त्यागृहेभ्यः ॥ इत्युप्तकेशेन स्नातेनाक्तेनाभ्यक्तेनालंकृतेन यज्ञोपवीतिना समेत्य जपति ।
text_mt:
"We have united with him who has arrived; let him avert from us our first misfortune.

Uninjured may we wander about; wander auspiciously to the quarters; / auspiciousness from the homes!"

Having met together with [the boy] who has had his hair shorn, has bathed, is anointed and smeared with salve, adorned, and wearing the sacred thread, he mutters [the verse].

sanskrit_iast: athāsmai vāsaḥ prayacchati yā akṛntanyā atanvanyā āvanyā avāharan yāścāgnyā devyo 'ntānabhito 'bhito 'tatananta tāstvā devyo jarase saṃvyayantvāyuṣmannidaṃ paridhatsva vāsaḥ || ityahataṃ vāsaḥparidhāpyānvārabhyādhārāvājyabhāgau hutvā-yaśeṣe dadhyānīya dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣamiti dadhi triḥ prāśnāti |
meaning: अथास्मै वासः प्रयच्छति या अकृन्तन्या अतन्वन्या आवन्या अवाहरन् याश्चाग्न्या देव्यो ऽन्तानभितो ऽभितो ऽततनन्त तास्त्वा देव्यो जरसे संव्ययन्त्वायुष्मन्निदं परिधत्स्व वासः ॥ इत्यहतं वासःपरिधाप्यान्वारभ्याधारावाज्यभागौ हुत्वा-यशेषे दध्यानीय दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषमिति दधि त्रिः प्राश्नाति ।
text_mt:
Then he hands him a garment:

"They who cut, they who stretched, they who wove, they who drew out [the threads], / and the divine women who extended the borders on all sides of the fire,

may those goddesses clothe you until old age; put on this garment, O long-lived one!"

Having made him put on an unwashed garment, having touched him from behind and offered the two portions of clarified butter, he pours curd into the remaining sacrificial butter and eats curd three times with the verse: "I have sung the praise of Dadhikrāvan..."

sanskrit_iast: nāmadheye prokte ''devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ hastaṃ gṛhṇāmyasāviti hastaṃ gṛhṇannāma gṛhṇāti prāṅmukhasya pratyaṅmukha ūrdhvastiṣṭhannāsīnasya dakṣiṇamuttānaṃ dakṣiṇena nīcārīktamariktena savitā te hastamagrahīdāsāvagnirācāryastava devasavitareṣate brahmacārī tvaṃ gopāya samāvṛtat | kasya brahmacāryasi | prāṇasya brahmacāryasi | kastvā kamupanayate | kāya tvā paridadāmi | kasmai tvā paridadāmi | tasmai tvā paridadāmi | bhagāya tvā paridadāmyaryamṇe tvā paridadāmi savitre tvā paridadāmi sarasvatyai tvā paridadāmīndrāgnibhyāṃ tvā paridadāmi viśvebhyastvā devebhyaḥ paridadāmisarvebhyastvā devebhyaḥ paridadāmīti paridadāti |
meaning: नामधेये प्रोक्ते ऽऽदेवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यां हस्तं गृह्णाम्यसाविति हस्तं गृह्णन्नाम गृह्णाति प्राङ्मुखस्य प्रत्यङ्मुख ऊर्ध्वस्तिष्ठन्नासीनस्य दक्षिणमुत्तानं दक्षिणेन नीचारीक्तमरिक्तेन सविता ते हस्तमग्रहीदासावग्निराचार्यस्तव देवसवितरेषते ब्रह्मचारी त्वं गोपाय समावृतत् । कस्य ब्रह्मचार्यसि । प्राणस्य ब्रह्मचार्यसि । कस्त्वा कमुपनयते । काय त्वा परिददामि । कस्मै त्वा परिददामि । तस्मै त्वा परिददामि । भगाय त्वा परिददाम्यर्यम्णे त्वा परिददामि सवित्रे त्वा परिददामि सरस्वत्यै त्वा परिददामीन्द्राग्निभ्यां त्वा परिददामि विश्वेभ्यस्त्वा देवेभ्यः परिददामिसर्वेभ्यस्त्वा देवेभ्यः परिददामीति परिददाति ।
text_mt:
When the name has been stated, he grasps his hand and takes his name, saying: "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I take your hand, N.N.!"—[the teacher] facing west, standing upright, [takes] the right, upturned hand with his own right hand facing down, not empty with not empty, while [the boy] sits facing east: "Savitṛ has grasped your hand, N.N.! Fire is your preceptor. Divine Savitṛ, this is your student; protect him until his return home! Whose student are you? You are the student of breath (prāṇa). Who initiates whom? To whom (ka) do I entrust you? To whom (kasmin) do I entrust you?

To that one I entrust you! I entrust you to Bhaga; I entrust you to Aryaman; I entrust you to Savitṛ; I entrust you to Sarasvatī; I entrust you to Indra and Agni; I entrust you to the All-gods; I entrust you to all the gods!"—thus he entrusts him.

sanskrit_iast: brahmaṇogranthirasi sa te mā visrasaditi hṛdayadeśamārabhya japati | prāṇānāṃgranthirasīti prāṇadeśam |
meaning: ब्रह्मणोग्रन्थिरसि स ते मा विस्रसदिति हृदयदेशमारभ्य जपति । प्राणानांग्रन्थिरसीति प्राणदेशम् ।
text_mt: Touching the region of the heart, he mutters: "You are the knot of brahman; may it not loosen for you." Touching the region of breath, [he mutters]: "You are the knot of the breaths."

sanskrit_iast: ṛtasya goptrī tapasastarutrī ghnatī rakṣaḥ sahamānā arātīḥ sānaḥsamagantamabhiparyyehi bhadre dharttāraste subhage mekhale māriṣāma || iti mauñjīṃ pṛthivīṃ triguṇāṃ mekhalāmādatte |
meaning: ऋतस्य गोप्त्री तपसस्तरुत्री घ्नती रक्षः सहमाना अरातीः सानःसमगन्तमभिपर्य्येहि भद्रे धर्त्तारस्ते सुभगे मेखले मारिषाम ॥ इति मौञ्जीं पृथिवीं त्रिगुणां मेखलामादत्ते ।
text_mt:
"Protectress of cosmic order, ferry across ascetic toil, slaying the demon, overpowering the adversaries,

having arrived, encircle us all around, O auspicious one; may we, wearing you, O fortunate girdle, not suffer harm!"

With this [mantra], he takes a threefold girdle made of muñja grass, [broad as] the earth.

sanskrit_iast: yuvāsuvāsā iti mekhalāṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ triḥ parivyayati |
meaning: युवासुवासा इति मेखलां प्रदक्षिणं त्रिः परिव्ययति ।
text_mt: With the verse "A youth, well-attired..." he wraps the girdle around [him] clockwise three times.
For a male, he ties three knots.

sanskrit_iast: iyaṃ duruktātparibādhamānā varṇaṃ purāṇaṃ punatīma āgāt prāṇāpānābhyāṃ balamābhajantī śivādevī subhage mekhale māriṣāma | iti tasyāṃ parivītāyāṃ japati mama vrate te hṛdayaṃ dadhātu mama cittamanucittaṃ te astu mama vācamekavrato juṣasva bṛhaspatiṣṭvā niyunaktu mahyam || iti |
meaning: इयं दुरुक्तात्परिबाधमाना वर्णं पुराणं पुनतीम आगात् प्राणापानाभ्यां बलमाभजन्ती शिवादेवी सुभगे मेखले मारिषाम । इति तस्यां परिवीतायां जपति मम व्रते ते हृदयं दधातु मम चित्तमनुचित्तं ते अस्तु मम वाचमेकव्रतो जुषस्व बृहस्पतिष्ट्वा नियुनक्तु मह्यम् ॥ इति ।
text_mt:
"Warding off ill speech, purifying the ancient color, this [girdle] has come to me, / imparting strength through in-breath and out-breath, a benign goddess; O fortunate girdle, may we not suffer harm!" / While she is being tied on, he mutters:

"May he place your heart in my vow; may your mind follow my mind; / take pleasure in my word with a single vow; may Bṛhaspati join you to me!"

sanskrit_iast: yajñiyasya vṛkṣasya daṇḍaṃ pradāya kṛṣṇājinaṃ cādityamupasthāpayati adhvanāmadhvapate śraiṣṭhyasya svastyasyādhvanaḥ pāramaśīya | taccakṣurdevahitaṃ purastācchukramuccarat || paśyema śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śatam | śṛṇuyāma śaradaḥ śataṃ prabravāma śaradaḥ śatam | adīnāḥ syāma śaradaḥ śataṃ bhūyaśca śaradaḥ śatāt || yā medhāpsaraḥsu gandharveṣu ca yanmanaḥ | daivī yā mānuṣī medhā sā māmāviśatāmihaiva || iti |
meaning: यज्ञियस्य वृक्षस्य दण्डं प्रदाय कृष्णाजिनं चादित्यमुपस्थापयति अध्वनामध्वपते श्रैष्ठ्यस्य स्वस्त्यस्याध्वनः पारमशीय । तच्चक्षुर्देवहितं पुरस्ताच्छुक्रमुच्चरत् ॥ पश्येम शरदः शतं जीवेम शरदः शतम् । शृणुयाम शरदः शतं प्रब्रवाम शरदः शतम् । अदीनाः स्याम शरदः शतं भूयश्च शरदः शतात् ॥ या मेधाप्सरःसु गन्धर्वेषु च यन्मनः । दैवी या मानुषी मेधा सा मामाविशतामिहैव ॥ इति ।
text_mt:
Having handed [him] a staff of a sacrificial tree and a black antelope skin, he makes him worship the Sun: "O lord of the pathways of pathways, may I attain the auspicious goal of this path of preeminence.

That eye established by the gods, bright, rising in the east:

may we see for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns; / may we hear for a hundred autumns; may we speak for a hundred autumns; / may we be unsubdued for a hundred autumns, and even more than a hundred autumns!

The intelligence that is in the Apsarases, and the mind that is in the Gandharvas, / the divine intelligence and that of humans, may that enter me right here!"

sanskrit_iast: abhidakṣiṇamānīyāgneḥ paścāt ehyaśmānamātiṣṭhāśmeva tvaṃ sthiro bhava | kṛṇvantu viśve devā āyuṣṭe śaradaḥ śatam || iti dakṣiṇena pādenāśmānamāsthāpayati |
meaning: अभिदक्षिणमानीयाग्नेः पश्चात् एह्यश्मानमातिष्ठाश्मेव त्वं स्थिरो भव । कृण्वन्तु विश्वे देवा आयुष्टे शरदः शतम् ॥ इति दक्षिणेन पादेनाश्मानमास्थापयति ।
text_mt:
Having led him around clockwise to the west of the fire:

"Come, step on the stone; be firm like a stone! / May all the gods make your life a hundred autumns!"

With this [verse] he makes him step upon a stone with his right foot.

sanskrit_iast: paścādagnermahadupastīrya sūpasthalaṃ kṛtvā prāṅāsīnaḥ pratyaṅṅāsīnāyānuvācayati gāyatrīṃ sāvitrimapi hyeke triṣṭubhamapi hyeke jagatīmomityapatkā vyāhṛtibhiśca |
meaning: पश्चादग्नेर्महदुपस्तीर्य सूपस्थलं कृत्वा प्राङासीनः प्रत्यङ्ङासीनायानुवाचयति गायत्रीं सावित्रिमपि ह्येके त्रिष्टुभमपि ह्येके जगतीमोमित्यपत्का व्याहृतिभिश्च ।
text_mt: Behind the fire, having spread out a large [mat] and made a good seat, sitting facing east, he recites to him who sits facing west the Gāyatrī verse dedicated to Savitṛ; according to some, also a Triṣṭubh; according to some, also a Jagatī; with 'Om' in case of misfortune, and with the sacred utterances.

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ triravagṛhṇīyāttāṃ dviravakṛtya tāṃ-sakṛtsamasyet pādaśor'dharcaśaḥ sarvāmantena |
meaning: तां त्रिरवगृह्णीयात्तां द्विरवकृत्य तां-सकृत्समस्येत् पादशोर्ऽधर्चशः सर्वामन्तेन ।
text_mt: He should divide it into three; having divided it into two, he should combine it once: by quarters, by half-verses, and finally the whole.

sanskrit_iast: yattisṛṇāṃ prātaranvāha yad dvayoryadekasyāḥ saṃ vatsare dvādaśāhe ṣaḍahe tryahe vā tasmātsadyo 'nūcyeti śrutiḥ |
meaning: यत्तिसृणां प्रातरन्वाह यद् द्वयोर्यदेकस्याः सं वत्सरे द्वादशाहे षडहे त्र्यहे वा तस्मात्सद्यो ऽनूच्येति श्रुतिः ।
text_mt: 'That which he recites of the three in the morning, which of the two, which of the one, [recited] in a year, in twelve days, in six days, or in three days, therefore it is to be recited immediately,' such is the Vedic revelation.

sanskrit_iast: varaṃ kartre dadāti kāṃsyaṃ vasanaṃ ca |
meaning: वरं कर्त्रे ददाति कांस्यं वसनं च ।
text_mt: He gives a choice gift to the officiant, a vessel of bell-metal and a garment.

sanskrit_iast: yasya tu medhākāmaḥ syātpalāśaṃ navanītenābhyājya tasya cchāyāyāṃ vācayet-suśravaḥ suśravā asi | yathā tvaṃ suśravaḥsuśravā asi evaṃ māṃ suśravaḥ sauśravaṃ kuru || yathā tvaṃ devānāṃ nidhipo asi evamahaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ vedānāṃ nidhipo bhūyāsam || iti |
meaning: यस्य तु मेधाकामः स्यात्पलाशं नवनीतेनाभ्याज्य तस्य च्छायायां वाचयेत्-सुश्रवः सुश्रवा असि । यथा त्वं सुश्रवःसुश्रवा असि एवं मां सुश्रवः सौश्रवं कुरु ॥ यथा त्वं देवानां निधिपो असि एवमहं मनुष्याणां वेदानां निधिपो भूयासम् ॥ इति ।
text_mt:
If he should desire intelligence for him, having smeared a palāśa [stick] with fresh butter, he should make him recite in its shadow: "O you of good renown, you are of good renown! / As you, O you of good renown, are of good renown, so make me, O you of good renown, to possess good renown!

As you are the guardian of the treasure of the gods, / so may I become the guardian of the treasure of the Vedas of humans!"

sanskrit_iast: a-teha vā ayameṣāṃ vedānāmekaṃ dvau trīn sarvānveti yamevaṃvidvāṃsamupanayatīti śrutiḥ |
meaning: अ-तेह वा अयमेषां वेदानामेकं द्वौ त्रीन् सर्वान्वेति यमेवंविद्वांसमुपनयतीति श्रुतिः ।
text_mt: 'This one surely [reaches the end] of these Vedas—one, two, three, or all—whom one initiates knowing thus,' such is the Vedic revelation.
Studenthood has been explained.

sanskrit_iast: atha bhaikṣaṃ carate mātaramevāgre yāścānyāḥ suhṛdo yāvatyo vā sannihitāḥ syuḥ |
meaning: अथ भैक्षं चरते मातरमेवाग्रे याश्चान्याः सुहृदो यावत्यो वा सन्निहिताः स्युः ।
text_mt: Then he begs alms: first from his mother, and whichever other female friends or as many as may be present.
He offers the alms to the preceptor; he should eat when permitted by him, such is the Vedic revelation.
Now the consecration of the four-Hotṛ rite [lasts] for a year.
He should sacrifice the four Hotṛ [formulas] pertaining to his own rite together with the six-Hotṛ and seven-Hotṛ [formulas].
At the end, having imparted the vow, he should make him recite the first two lessons from the beginning.
In this very way he should sacrifice the deconsecration.
Now the consecration of the fire-altar rite [lasts] for twelve nights.

sanskrit_iast: yuñjānaḥ prathamaṃ mana itiyaṣṭau hutvākūtamagniṃ prayuñjaṃ svāheti ṣaḍ juhoti viśvodevasya neturiti saptamīm |
meaning: युञ्जानः प्रथमं मन इतियष्टौ हुत्वाकूतमग्निं प्रयुञ्जं स्वाहेति षड् जुहोति विश्वोदेवस्य नेतुरिति सप्तमीम् ।
text_mt: Having offered eight [oblations] with 'Yoking first the mind...,' he offers six with 'To the fire of intention, yoking, svāhā,' and the seventh with 'Of the divine guide of all...'
Having imparted the vow, he should make him recite the first eight lessons from the beginning.
At the three daily pressings he should fetch water, three jars each time.

sanskrit_iast: ekena vāsasāntarhitāyāṃ bhūmau śayīta bhasmani karīṣe sikatāsu vā |
meaning: एकेन वाससान्तर्हितायां भूमौ शयीत भस्मनि करीषे सिकतासु वा ।
text_mt: With a single garment he should sleep on the bare ground, on ashes, on dry cow dung, or on sand.
When it is completed, having sacrificed with a ghee-covered rice cake, he should recite the Vātsa [hymn].
Then he should feed the Brāhmaṇas with ghee-covered rice cakes.
In this very way he should sacrifice the deconsecration.
Now the consecration of the horse-sacrifice rite [lasts] for twelve nights.

sanskrit_iast: vaitasamidhmamupasamādhāya navamenānuvākena hutvā ṣaṣṭhenopasthāpya vrataṃ pradāyādita ekaviṃśatyanuvākānanuvācayet |
meaning: वैतसमिध्ममुपसमाधाय नवमेनानुवाकेन हुत्वा षष्ठेनोपस्थाप्य व्रतं प्रदायादित एकविंशत्यनुवाकाननुवाचयेत् ।
text_mt: Having placed fuel sticks of reed on the fire, having offered with the ninth lesson, having praised [the fire] with the sixth, and having imparted the vow, he should make him recite twenty-one lessons from the beginning.
At each of the three daily pressings he should fetch fodder for the horse, three bundles each time.

sanskrit_iast: ekena vāsasānantarhitāyāṃ bhūmau śayīta bhasmani karīṣe sikatāsu vā |
meaning: एकेन वाससानन्तर्हितायां भूमौ शयीत भस्मनि करीषे सिकतासु वा ।
text_mt: Wearing a single garment, he should sleep on the bare ground, on ashes, dry cowdung, or sand.

sanskrit_iast: yā oṣadhayaḥsamānyāyanti punantu mā pitaro 'gnermanvā iti caturbhiranuvākairapobhimantrya snānamācaret |
meaning: या ओषधयःसमान्यायन्ति पुनन्तु मा पितरो ऽग्नेर्मन्वा इति चतुर्भिरनुवाकैरपोभिमन्त्र्य स्नानमाचरेत् ।
text_mt: With the four anuvākas, 'The plants that come together...', 'May the ancestors purify me...', and 'Of Agni, Manu...', he should consecrate the water and perform his ritual bath.
In the very same way he should offer the deconsecration [oblations].
He should make [him] recite the fourteen anuvākas [beginning with] 'Grass with teeth...'.
When he intends to study the secret doctrine, the Pravargya rite [is performed].
At the instruction, as explained previously.
From the beginning, he should make [him] recite twenty-five anuvākas.
The threefold-Veda vow is explained by initiation.
From the beginning, he should make [him] recite three anuvākas.
The vows are explained; the vows are explained.

With [the verse], 'Loosen the highest bond of Varuṇa...', he unties the girdle.

Thus ends the twenty-third section of the Maitrāyaṇīya Mānavagṛhyasūtra; the first book is complete.

sanskrit_iast: prathamaḥ puruṣaḥ samāptaḥ || saptame navame vopāyanam || āgantrā samaganmahī prathamamarttiṃ yuyotu naḥ | ariṣṭāḥ saṃceramahi svasti caratādiśaḥ | svastyāgrahebhyaḥ || ityuptakeśena snātenāktenābhyaktenālaṃkṛtena yajñopavītināsametya japati || athāsmaivāsaḥ prayacchati yā akṛntanyā atanvanyā āvanyā avāharan | yāśca gnā devyo 'ntānabhito 'tatananta || tāsvā devyo jarame saṃ vyayantvāyuṣmānidaṃ paridhatsva vāsaḥ || ityahataṃ vāsaḥ || pu. iyaṃ duruktātparibādhamānā varṇaṃ purāṇaṃ punatīma āgāt | prāṇāpānābhyāṃ balamābhajantī śivā devī subhage mekhale māriṣāma || iti tasyāṃ parivītāyāṃ japati mama vrate te hṛdayaṃ dadhātu mama cittamanucittaṃ te astu mama vācamekakavrato juṣasva bṛhaspatiṣṭvā niyunaktu mahyam || iti || yajñiyasya vṛkṣasya daṇḍaṃ pradāya kṛṣṇājinaṃ cādityamupasthāpayati adhvānamadhvapate śraiṣṭhyasya svastasyādhvanaḥ pāramaśīya | taccakṣurdevahitaṃ purastaccukramuccarat || śṛṇuyāma śaradaḥ śataṃ jīvema śaradaḥ śatam | adīnāḥ syāma śaradaḥ śataṃ meaning: प्रथमः पुरुषः समाप्तः ॥ सप्तमे नवमे वोपायनम् ॥ आगन्त्रा समगन्मही प्रथममर्त्तिं युयोतु नः । अरिष्टाः संचेरमहि स्वस्ति चरतादिशः । स्वस्त्याग्रहेभ्यः ॥ इत्युप्तकेशेन स्नातेनाक्तेनाभ्यक्तेनालंकृतेन यज्ञोपवीतिनासमेत्य जपति ॥ अथास्मैवासः प्रयच्छति या अकृन्तन्या अतन्वन्या आवन्या अवाहरन् । याश्च ग्ना देव्यो ऽन्तानभितो ऽततनन्त ॥ तास्वा देव्यो जरमे सं व्ययन्त्वायुष्मानिदं परिधत्स्व वासः ॥ इत्यहतं वासः ॥ पु. इयं दुरुक्तात्परिबाधमाना वर्णं पुराणं पुनतीम आगात् । प्राणापानाभ्यां बलमाभजन्ती शिवा देवी सुभगे मेखले मारिषाम ॥ इति तस्यां परिवीतायां जपति मम व्रते ते हृदयं दधातु मम चित्तमनुचित्तं ते अस्तु मम वाचमेककव्रतो जुषस्व बृहस्पतिष्ट्वा नियुनक्तु मह्यम् ॥ इति ॥ यज्ञियस्य वृक्षस्य दण्डं प्रदाय कृष्णाजिनं चादित्यमुपस्थापयति अध्वानमध्वपते श्रैष्ठ्यस्य स्वस्तस्याध्वनः पारमशीय । तच्चक्षुर्देवहितं पुरस्तच्चुक्रमुच्चरत् ॥ शृणुयाम शरदः शतं जीवेम शरदः शतम् । अदीनाः स्याम शरदः शतं भूयश्च शरदः शतात् ॥ या मेधाप्सरःसु गन्धर्वेषु च यन्मनः । दैवी या मानुषी मेधा सा मामाविशतामिहैव ॥ इति ॥ अभिदक्षिणमानीयाग्नेः पश्चात् एह्यश्मानमातिष्ठाश्मेव त्वं स्थिरो भव । कृण्वन्तु विश्वे देवा आयुष्चे शरदः शतम् ॥ इति दक्षिणेन पादेनाश्मानमास्थापयति ॥ पश्चादग्नेर्महदुपस्तीर्य सूपस्थलं कृत्वा प्राङासीनः प्रत्यङ्ङासीनायानुवाचयति गायत्रीं सावित्रीमपि ह्येके त्रिष्टुभमपि ह्येके जगतीमोमित्युत्त्का व्याहृतिभिश्च ॥ तां त्रिरवगृङ्णीयात्तां द्विरवकृत्य तां सकृत्समस्येत् पादशोर्ऽधर्चशः सर्वामन्तेन ॥ यत्तिसृणां प्रातरन्वाह यत् द्वयोर्यदेकस्याः संवत्सरे द्वादशाहे षडहे त्र्यहे वा तस्मात्सद्यो ऽनूच्यति श्रुतिः ॥ वरं कर्त्रे ददाति कांस्यं वसनं च ॥ यस्य तु मेधाकामः स्यात्पलाशं नवनीतेनाभ्यज्य तस्य छायायांवाचयेत् । सुश्रवः सुश्रवा असि यथा त्वंसुश्रवः सुश्रवा असि एवं मां सुश्रवः सौश्रवसं कुरु ॥ यथा त्वं देवानां वेदानां निधिपो असि । एवमहं मनुष्याणां वेदानां निधिपो भूयासमिति ॥ अधीतेह वा अयमेषां वेदानामेकं द्वौ त्रीन् सर्वान्वेति यमेनं विद्वांसमुपनयतीति श्रुतिः ॥ व्याख्यातं ब्रह्मचर्यम् ॥ अथ भैक्षं चरते मातरमेवाग्रे याश्चान्याः सुहृदो यावत्यो वा सन्निहिताः स्युः ॥ आचार्याय भैक्षमुपकल्पयते तेनानुज्ञातो वा भुञ्जीतेति श्रुतिः ॥ औद्वाहिकं प्रेतपिता शालाग्निंकुर्वीत ।
text_mt:
The approaching [for initiation takes place] in the seventh or in the ninth [year]. // 1

With the comer we have met; let him drive away our first misfortune.
Uninjured may we wander together; go safely toward all directions!
Safety from afflictions!

Having met him whose hair has been shorn, who has taken a ritual bath, who is anointed, rubbed with fragrant oil, adorned, and wearing the sacred thread, he mutters [this]. // 1.22.2 // Now he gives him a garment:

They who cut, they who stretched, they who wove, they who took down,

And the divine wives who stretched the borders all around;

May those goddesses clothe you unto old age; do you, full of long life, put on this garment!

Ward off bad speech, purifying the ancient color, this [girdle] has come to me;
Bestowing strength on inhalation and exhalation, auspicious goddess, fortunate girdle, may we not suffer harm!

When that [girdle] has been fastened around [him], he mutters:

May he place your heart in my vow; may your mind follow my mind;

Delight in my word, sole-vowed; may Bṛhaspati unite you to me!

Having handed [him] a staff of sacrificial wood and a black antelope skin, he makes him worship the Sun:

Lord of the road, of the road of preeminence, may I reach the end of this safe road!

That eye established by the gods, bright, rising in the east,

May we see for a hundred autumns, may we live for a hundred autumns,

May we not be destitute for a hundred autumns, and even more than a hundred autumns!

The wisdom that is in the Apsarases, and the mind that is in the Gandharvas,

The divine and human wisdom, may that enter into me right here!

Leading [him] clockwise behind the fire:

Come, step upon the stone; be steadfast like a stone!
May all the gods make your lifespan a hundred autumns!

[Blank]

With this [verse] he makes him step upon the stone with his right foot. // 12

Behind the fire, having spread a large layer [of grass] and made a comfortable seat, seated facing east, he makes [the student] who is seated facing west recite the Gāyatrī verse dedicated to Savitṛ; according to some, also the Triṣṭubh; according to some, also the Jagatī, having uttered 'Om' and with the sacred utterances. // 13

He should divide it [and teach it] three times; having divided it twice, he should join it together once: quarter-verse by quarter-verse, half-verse by half-verse, and finally the whole [verse]. // 14

Whether [he teaches] in three mornings, in two, or in one, in a year, in twelve days, in six days, or in three days; 'therefore, it should be recited immediately,' says the Vedic revelation. // 15

He gives a gift of choice to the performer: a bronze vessel and a garment. // 16

For him, however, who desires intellectual vigor, having anointed a Palāśa stick with fresh butter, he should make him recite in its shade:

Just as you, O well-renowned one, are of good renown, so, O well-renowned one, make me well-renowned!

Just as you are the guardian of the treasury of the Vedas for the gods,

So may I become the guardian of the treasury of the Vedas for human beings! // — thus. // 17

'Indeed, he who initiates this knowing one studies one, two, three, or all of these Vedas,' says the Vedic revelation. // 18

sanskrit_iast: anyatra tataḥ prete pitari prajvalanto 'gniṃ jāgarayeyuḥ parvaṇi jyaitsne puṇye nakṣatre 'nyatra navamyāḥ |
meaning: अन्यत्र ततः प्रेते पितरि प्रज्वलन्तो ऽग्निं जागरयेयुः पर्वणि ज्यैत्स्ने पुण्ये नक्षत्रे ऽन्यत्र नवम्याः ।
text_mt:
Studenthood has been explained. // 19

Now he goes about for alms: first to his mother, then to other female friends, or as many as may be present. // 20

He delivers the alms to the preceptor, or he should eat permitted by him, says the Vedic revelation. // 21

One whose father is dead should make the hall fire the nuptial fire.

Elsewhere than that, when the father is dead, burning [firebrands] they should keep awake the fire on a new or full moon day during the bright fortnight, under an auspicious constellation, other than the ninth [tithi].
Having bathed, pure, wearing an unwashed garment,
Restraining his speech, he watches over the churning stick [and lower kindling wood].
In an open space, having ground whole barley grains, he stirs a thick beverage with a sugarcane shoot, without touching it [with his hand].

sanskrit_iast: hiraṇyapāṇiṃ savitāraṃ vāyumindraṃ prajāpatim | viśvāndevānaṅgiraso havāmahe amuṃ kravyādaṃ śamayantvagnim || iti manthenāgnimavasiñcati |
meaning: हिरण्यपाणिं सवितारं वायुमिन्द्रं प्रजापतिम् । विश्वान्देवानङ्गिरसो हवामहे अमुं क्रव्यादं शमयन्त्वग्निम् ॥ इति मन्थेनाग्निमवसिञ्चति ।
text_mt:
The golden-handed Savitṛ, Vāyu, Indra, Prajāpati,

All the gods, the Aṅgirases we invoke:

May they appease that flesh-consuming fire!

With these words, he sprinkles the fire with a mash.

sanskrit_iast: somo rājā vibhajatūbhāgnirvvibhājayan | ihaivāstu havyavāhano 'gniḥ kravyādaṃ nudasva || iti kaṭe kṛtāyāṃ vāgniṃsamāropya prahiṇoti |
meaning: सोमो राजा विभजतूभाग्निर्व्विभाजयन् । इहैवास्तु हव्यवाहनो ऽग्निः क्रव्यादं नुदस्व ॥ इति कटे कृतायां वाग्निंसमारोप्य प्रहिणोति ।

sanskrit_iast: kravyādamagniṃ prahiṇomi dūraṃ yamarājyaṃ gacchatu ripravāhaḥ | ihaivāyamitaro jātavedā devebhyo havyā vahatu prajānan || ityagnimādāya dakṣiṇā pratyagharanti |
meaning: क्रव्यादमग्निं प्रहिणोमि दूरं यमराज्यं गच्छतु रिप्रवाहः । इहैवायमितरो जातवेदा देवेभ्यो हव्या वहतु प्रजानन् ॥ इत्यग्निमादाय दक्षिणा प्रत्यघरन्ति ।
text_mt:
“I send the corpse-devouring fire far away; let the carrier of defilement go to Yama's realm.

Right here let this other Jātavedas, knowing [the way], convey oblations to the gods.”

With these words, having taken the fire, they carry it away toward the south-west.
They go along with the implements.

sanskrit_iast: svakṛta iriṇe sīse malimlucāmahe śiromimupabarhaṇe | avyāmasitāyāmṛṣṭvāstaṃ pretasudānavaḥ || iti sīsamupadhānyenyasyādhyadhi |
meaning: स्वकृत इरिणे सीसे मलिम्लुचामहे शिरोमिमुपबर्हणे । अव्यामसितायामृष्ट्वास्तं प्रेतसुदानवः ॥ इति सीसमुपधान्येन्यस्याध्यधि ।
text_mt:
“Into lead we wipe off our defilement, the head on a bolster.

Having wiped it away into the dark ewe, go back home, O bounteous ones!”

With these words, having placed lead upon a pillow, [he places it] upon each [implement].

sanskrit_iast: dhāmno dhāmna iti tisṛbhiḥ parogoṣṭhaṃ mārjayante |
meaning: धाम्नो धाम्न इति तिसृभिः परोगोष्ठं मार्जयन्ते ।
text_mt: With the three [verses beginning with] “From abode to abode,” they cleanse themselves beyond the cattle-pen.
Without looking back, they return.

sanskrit_iast: nalairvetasaśākhayā vā padāni lopayante mṛtyoḥ padāni lopayante yadetaddrāghīrya āyuḥ pratiraṃ dadhānaḥ | āpyāyamānāḥ prajayā dhanena śuddhāḥ pūtā bhavantu yajñiyāsaḥ |
meaning: नलैर्वेतसशाखया वा पदानि लोपयन्ते मृत्योः पदानि लोपयन्ते यदेतद्द्राघीर्य आयुः प्रतिरं दधानः । आप्यायमानाः प्रजया धनेन शुद्धाः पूता भवन्तु यज्ञियासः ।
text_mt:
With reeds or with a branch of the reed-cane, they efface the footprints—

“They efface the footprints of death as they come, prolonging a longer span of life, / swelling with offspring and wealth, let them become clean, purified, worthy of sacrifice.”
“Take hold of the draft-ox, the float, by which Saramā slipped down, barking—”
Having raised and sprinkled the fire-place, he strews down the earthy substances belonging to the setting up of the sacred fires, with the exception of saline soil and sand.

sanskrit_iast: araṇibhyāmagniṃ mathitvā hiraṇyaśakalaṃ ca nyupya prāgudayādupasthakṛto bhūriti jvalantamādadhāti |
meaning: अरणिभ्यामग्निं मथित्वा हिरण्यशकलं च न्युप्य प्रागुदयादुपस्थकृतो भूरिति ज्वलन्तमादधाति ।
text_mt: Having churned the fire with two kindling-sticks and scattered a gold piece, sitting on his heels, he places the blazing [fire] before sunrise, [reciting,] “Bhūḥ!”
A cow, a garment, and a bronze vessel are the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit_iast: prāgudañcaṃ lakṣaṇamuddhatyāvokṣya sthaṇḍilaṃ gomayenopalipyamaṇḍalaṃ caturasraṃvāgniṃ nirmathyābhimukhaṃ praṇayet |
meaning: प्रागुदञ्चं लक्षणमुद्धत्यावोक्ष्य स्थण्डिलं गोमयेनोपलिप्यमण्डलं चतुरस्रंवाग्निं निर्मथ्याभिमुखं प्रणयेत् ।
text_mt: Having raised [the earth] and sprinkled an area pointing east or north-east, having smeared a sacrificial mound with cow-dung in a circle or square, he should churn the fire and carry it forward facing [the mound].
Having produced two strainers of darbha grass with the appropriate mantra, he cooks a pot-cooked offering sacred to Agni.

sanskrit_iast: pavitrāntarhite 'pa ānīya taṇḍulānopya mekṣaṇena pradakṣiṇaṃ paryāyuvañjīva taṇḍulaṃ śrapayati |
meaning: पवित्रान्तर्हिते ऽप आनीय तण्डुलानोप्य मेक्षणेन प्रदक्षिणं पर्यायुवञ्जीव तण्डुलं श्रपयति ।
text_mt: Having poured water [into the pot] holding the strainers between, having thrown in the rice grains, stirring them clockwise with the stirring-stick, he cooks the whole-grain rice.
Having poured clarified butter over the cooked [offering] with unpurified [ghee] or with purified fresh butter, he takes it off toward the north.

sanskrit_iast: imaṃ stomamarhata ityagniṃ parisamuhya paryukṣya paristīrya paścādagnerekavaddarhistṛṇāti |
meaning: इमं स्तोममर्हत इत्यग्निं परिसमुह्य पर्युक्ष्य परिस्तीर्य पश्चादग्नेरेकवद्दर्हिस्तृणाति ।
text_mt: With “Deserving of this praise…,” having swept around the fire, sprinkled water around the fire, and strewn grass around the fire, he strews the sacred grass behind the fire as a single layer.

Having drawn out darbha blades with their tips pointing north and east, he covers the northern ones with the southern ones in front of the fire, and the northern ones with the southern ones [in like manner].
To the south of the fire he strews [grass] for the Brāhmaṇa [priest], another for the sacrificer, and in the western half for the wife.

sanskrit_iast: uttarataḥ saṃstīrṇe pavitre sruksruvāvājyasthālīṃ prakṣālya saṃstīrṇe dve dve prayunakti |
meaning: उत्तरतः संस्तीर्णे पवित्रे स्रुक्स्रुवावाज्यस्थालीं प्रक्षाल्य संस्तीर्णे द्वे द्वे प्रयुनक्ति ।
text_mt: On the strewn [grass] to the north, having washed the two strainers, the two spoons—the sruc and sruva—and the pot for clarified butter, he arranges them two by two on the strewn [grass].

sanskrit_iast: tūṣṇīṃ dakṣiṇata ājyaṃ nirūpya mantravatparyagniṃ kṛtvā tūṣṇīṃ sruksruvau saṃmṛjyādabdhena tvā cakṣuṣāvekṣa iti patnyājyāmavekṣate |
meaning: तूष्णीं दक्षिणत आज्यं निरूप्य मन्त्रवत्पर्यग्निं कृत्वा तूष्णीं स्रुक्स्रुवौ संमृज्यादब्धेन त्वा चक्षुषावेक्ष इति पत्न्याज्यामवेक्षते ।
text_mt: Silently setting down the clarified butter to the south, having moved the fire around it with a mantra, silently wiping the sruc and sruva, the wife looks at the clarified butter with, “With unblinking eye I look at you…”
Having silently placed it over the fire and taken it off, setting it down behind the fire, having purified it with a mantra, he looks at it.
The sacrificer looks at the clarified butter with, “You are splendor!”
Having placed the sruva in the pot for clarified butter, he brings it along in front of the pot-cooked offering, and behind [it] the stirring-stick.

sanskrit_iast: tūṣṇīṃ prāñcamidhmamupasamādhāya brahmāṇamāmantrya oṃ juhudhītyukte dakṣiṇena hastenāntareṇa jānunī prāṅāsīna ādhārau juhoti prājāpatyamuttarārdhe prāñcaṃ manasā aindraṃ dakṣiṇārddhe prāñcameva |
meaning: तूष्णीं प्राञ्चमिध्ममुपसमाधाय ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्य ओं जुहुधीत्युक्ते दक्षिणेन हस्तेनान्तरेण जानुनी प्राङासीन आधारौ जुहोति प्राजापत्यमुत्तरार्धे प्राञ्चं मनसा ऐन्द्रं दक्षिणार्द्धे प्राञ्चमेव ।
text_mt: Silently adding kindling pointing eastward, addressing the Brahman priest [and] when told, “Om, make the offering,” sitting facing east with his knees between [his arms], he pours the two foundation libations with his right hand: the one sacred to Prajāpati in the northern half pointing east mentally, and the one sacred to Indra in the southern half pointing east.
Then he offers the two portions of clarified butter: the one sacred to Agni in the northern half, the one sacred to Soma in the southern half, equal and not diagonal.

sanskrit_iast: yukto vaha yadākūtamiti dvābhyāmagniṃ yojayitvā nakṣatramiṣṭvā nakṣatradevatāṃ yajettithiṃ tithidevatāmṛtamṛtudevatāṃ ca |
meaning: युक्तो वह यदाकूतमिति द्वाभ्यामग्निं योजयित्वा नक्षत्रमिष्ट्वा नक्षत्रदेवतां यजेत्तिथिं तिथिदेवतामृतमृतुदेवतां च ।
text_mt: Having harnessed the fire with the two [verses], “Harnessed, carry…” and “Whatever intention…,” having sacrificed to the lunar mansion, he should sacrifice to the deity of the lunar mansion, to the lunar day, to the deity of the lunar day, to the season, and to the deity of the season.

sanskrit_iast: upastīryāpa upaspṛśya mekṣaṇena sthālīpākasyāvadyati madhyāt pūrvārddhād dvitīyaṃ paścārddhāttṛtīyaṃ yadi pañcāvadānasya |
meaning: उपस्तीर्याप उपस्पृश्य मेक्षणेन स्थालीपाकस्यावद्यति मध्यात् पूर्वार्द्धाद् द्वितीयं पश्चार्द्धात्तृतीयं यदि पञ्चावदानस्य ।
text_mt: Having made an under-layer [of clarified butter] and touched water, he cuts off portions of the pot-cooked offering with the stirring-stick: from the middle, a second from the eastern half, and a third from the western half if it is a fivefold-cut offering.
Having poured clarified butter over the portion cut off, he pours clarified butter back over the pot-cooked offering.
He offers in the center with, “To Agni, svāhā!”
With “You who are of the gods…” [he offers the portion] of the offering to Rudra.

sanskrit_iast: jayānhutvājāyasya sviṣṭakṛte samavadyatyuttarārddhātsakṛd dvimātram | dvirvā yadi pañcāvadānasya |
meaning: जयान्हुत्वाजायस्य स्विष्टकृते समवद्यत्युत्तरार्द्धात्सकृद् द्विमात्रम् । द्विर्वा यदि पञ्चावदानस्य ।
text_mt: Having offered the Jaya oblations, he cuts off a portion for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt from the northern half once, of double measure; or twice, if it is a fivefold-cut offering.
Having twice poured clarified butter over the portion cut off, he does not pour clarified butter back over the pot-cooked offering from then on.
With “To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!” he offers [the portion] separately in the north-eastern part.

sanskrit_iast: mekṣaṇaṃ darbhāṃścādhāyānumatibhyāṃvyāhṛtibhiśca tvaṃ no agne sa tvaṃ no agne ayāścāgne 'sītyetābhirjuhuyāt |
meaning: मेक्षणं दर्भांश्चाधायानुमतिभ्यांव्याहृतिभिश्च त्वं नो अग्ने स त्वं नो अग्ने अयाश्चाग्ने ऽसीत्येताभिर्जुहुयात् ।
text_mt:
Having placed on [the fire] the stirring-stick and the darbha grass, with the two Anumati verses, with the sacred utterances, and with “You, O Agni, to us…,” “So you, O Agni, to us…”,

and with “You are tireless, O Agni…,” he should make offerings with these.

sanskrit_iast: vi te muñcāmi raśanāṃ vi raśmīnīti ca dutvā pavitre 'nu prahṛtyājyenābhijuhoti |
meaning: वि ते मुञ्चामि रशनां वि रश्मीनीति च दुत्वा पवित्रे ऽनु प्रहृत्याज्येनाभिजुहोति ।
text_mt: And having offered with “I loosen your halter, your reins…,” having thrown the two strainers into [the fire] afterward, he makes an oblation over it with clarified butter.

meaning: एधो ऽस्येधीषीमहीति समिधमादधाति समिदसि समेधिषीमहीति द्वितीयाम् ।
text_mt: He places a firewood stick [on the fire] with, “You are kindling; may we kindle,” and a second with, “You are kindling; may we thrive.”
He worships [the fire] with, “I have moved along the waters today…”
He should sprinkle himself with the verses beginning with “O Waters, you are wholesome…”
By this pot-cooked offering, all pot-cooked offerings are explained.

sanskrit_iast: agnaye svāheti sāyaṃ juhoti prajāpataya iti dvitīyām |
meaning: अग्नये स्वाहेति सायं जुहोति प्रजापतय इति द्वितीयाम् ।
text_mt: He offers in the evening with, “To Agni, svāhā!” and a second with, “To Prajāpati…”

sanskrit_iast: sūryāya svāheti prātaḥ prajāpataya iti dvitīyām |
meaning: सूर्याय स्वाहेति प्रातः प्रजापतय इति द्वितीयाम् ।
text_mt: In the morning with, “To Sūrya, svāhā!” and a second with, “To Prajāpati…”

sanskrit_iast: agnīṣomīyaḥ sthālīpākaḥ paurṇamāsyāmaindrāgno 'māvāsyāyāmubhayatra cāgneyaḥ āgantuḥ pūrvaḥ paurṇamāsyāmuttaromāvāsyāyām |
meaning: अग्नीषोमीयः स्थालीपाकः पौर्णमास्यामैन्द्राग्नो ऽमावास्यायामुभयत्र चाग्नेयः आगन्तुः पूर्वः पौर्णमास्यामुत्तरोमावास्यायाम् ।
text_mt: The pot-cooked offering to Agni and Soma is on the full moon, the one to Indra and Agni on the new moon, and on both occasions the one to Agni; an additional offering comes first on the full moon and second on the new moon.
On the full moon day of Āśvayuja, he brings along a pot-cooked offering in addition to the daily morning pot-cooked offerings.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāgniṃrudraṃ paśupatimīśānaṃ tryambakaṃ śaradaṃ praṣātakaṃ gā iti yajati |
meaning: तस्याग्निंरुद्रं पशुपतिमीशानं त्र्यम्बकं शरदं प्रषातकं गा इति यजति ।
text_mt: In that [sacrifice], he offers to Agni, Rudra, Paśupati, Īśāna, Tryambaka, Autumn, the curd-and-butter mixture (praṣātaka), and the cows.

sanskrit_iast: dadhighṛtamiśraḥ praṣātakastasyā no mitrāvaruṇā pravāhaveti ca hutvāmbhaḥ sthāmbho vo bhakṣīyeti gāḥ prāśāpayati |
meaning: दधिघृतमिश्रः प्रषातकस्तस्या नो मित्रावरुणा प्रवाहवेति च हुत्वाम्भः स्थाम्भो वो भक्षीयेति गाः प्राशापयति ।
text_mt: The praṣātaka is a mixture of curds and clarified butter. Having offered of it with: 'May Mitra and Varuṇa come to us...' and 'Flow forward...', he causes the cows to consume it, saying: 'You are water, may I enjoy water from you.'
He should feed Brāhmaṇas with food prepared with clarified butter.
One should not eat of the new grain without having offered the first-fruits sacrifice (āgrayaṇa).

sanskrit_iast: parvaṇyāgrayaṇaṃ kurvīta vasante yavānāṃ śaradi vrīhīṇām |
meaning: पर्वण्याग्रयणं कुर्वीत वसन्ते यवानां शरदि व्रीहीणाम् ।
text_mt: He should perform the first-fruits sacrifice on a joint of the lunar phases: in spring of barley, in autumn of rice.

sanskrit_iast: agrapākasya payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti sajūrdyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ svāhā sajūḥ somāya svāheti |
meaning: अग्रपाकस्य पयसि स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा तस्य जुहोति सजूर्द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां स्वाहा सजूः सोमाय स्वाहेति ।
text_mt: Having cooked a pot-cooked offering of the first produce in milk, he offers of it with: 'Together with Heaven and Earth, svāhā! Together with Soma, svāhā!'
In autumn, [an offering] of millet to Soma; in spring, of bamboo seeds; or in both cases with clarified butter.
A first-born calf is the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit_iast: brāhmaṇa eva haviḥ śeṣaṃ bhujjīteti śrutiḥ |
meaning: ब्राह्मण एव हविः शेषं भुज्जीतेति श्रुतिः ।
text_mt: 'Only a Brāhmaṇa should eat the remainder of the oblation'—thus says the Vedic revelation.
When intending to sacrifice with an animal, he attends to the fire according to the ritual procedure of a domestic sacrifice.
[The procedure is] like that of an animal sacrifice, silently, except for the procedure of offerings to the deities.

sanskrit_iast: prokṣyānumānyopapāyya paryagniṃ kṛtvā śāmitraṃ praṇīya vapāśrapaṇībhyāmudañcaṃ prakramamāṇamanvārabhante |
meaning: प्रोक्ष्यानुमान्योपपाय्य पर्यग्निं कृत्वा शामित्रं प्रणीय वपाश्रपणीभ्यामुदञ्चं प्रक्रममाणमन्वारभन्ते ।
text_mt: Having sprinkled [the animal], obtained consent, brought it near, carried fire around it, brought forward the slaughtering fire, and set it advancing northward with the two omentum-cooking spits, they touch it from behind.
He looks on while it is being suffocated.

sanskrit_iast: saṃjñaptaṃsnapayitvā yathādaivataṃ vapāmutkṛtya śrapayitvā'dhārāvājyabhāgau hutvā jātavedo vapayā gaccha devāṃstvaṃhi hotā prathamo babhūva | ghṛtasyāgne tanvā saṃbhava satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā | iti vapāṃ juhoti |
meaning: संज्ञप्तंस्नपयित्वा यथादैवतं वपामुत्कृत्य श्रपयित्वाऽधारावाज्यभागौ हुत्वा जातवेदो वपया गच्छ देवांस्त्वंहि होता प्रथमो बभूव । घृतस्याग्ने तन्वा संभव सत्याः सन्तु यजमानस्य कामाः स्वाहा । इति वपां जुहोति ।
text_mt:
Having washed it once suffocated, cut out the omentum according to the deity, cooked it, and offered the two butter portions, [with the verse]:
'O Jātavedas, go to the gods with the omentum; for you became the first Hotṛ!
Combine with the body of clarified butter, O Agni; may the desires of the sacrificer come true, svāhā!'—with this,
[He offers] the two omentum-sticks with: 'Svāhā! Svāhā!'
He associates a pot-cooked offering [with it], dedicated to the same deity as the animal.
The two butter portions are offered for it.

sanskrit_iast: pāśubandhikānāmavadānānāṃ rasasyāvadāya daivataiḥ pracarya vasāhomaśeṣeṇa diśaḥ pratijayati yathā vājinena vanaspatimājyasya |
meaning: पाशुबन्धिकानामवदानानां रसस्यावदाय दैवतैः प्रचर्य वसाहोमशेषेण दिशः प्रतिजयति यथा वाजिनेन वनस्पतिमाज्यस्य ।
text_mt: Having cut off the juice of the portions of the animal sacrifice, proceeded with the deities, and with the remainder of the fat-offering, he conquers the directions, just as [he does] with the curd-broth [or] with clarified butter to Vanaspati.
Having offered the Jaya offerings, he cuts off portions from the three limbs for Sviṣṭakṛt.
The remainder has been explained by the pot-cooked offering.
An animal indeed is the sacrificial fee for an animal [sacrifice].
In autumn is the spit-ox sacrifice (śūlagava) dedicated to Rudra.

sanskrit_iast: prāgudīcyāṃ diśi grāmasyā sakāśe niśi gavāṃ madhye taṣṭo yūpaḥ |
meaning: प्रागुदीच्यां दिशि ग्रामस्या सकाशे निशि गवां मध्ये तष्टो यूपः ।
text_mt: In the northeast direction near the village, at night in the midst of the cows, a sacrificial post is carved.

sanskrit_iast: prāk sviṣṭakṛto 'ṣṭhau śoṇitapuṭān namaste rudramanyava iti prabhṛtibhiraṣṭabhiranuvākairdikṣvantardikṣu copaharet |
meaning: प्राक् स्विष्टकृतो ऽष्ठौ शोणितपुटान् नमस्ते रुद्रमन्यव इति प्रभृतिभिरष्टभिरनुवाकैर्दिक्ष्वन्तर्दिक्षु चोपहरेत् ।
text_mt: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt, he should offer eight leaf-cups of blood in the cardinal and intermediate directions with the eight sections beginning with 'Homage to your anger, O Rudra...'
He should bury the remainder in the ground, even the skin.
Some say the domestic animals for sacrifice have no sacrificial post.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the ritual for firm horses.
On the full moon of Āśvayuja.
The officiating priest is unmaimed, bathed, pure, and wearing an unwashed garment.

sanskrit_iast: prāgastamayānniṣkramyottarato grāmasya purastādvā śucau deśe 'śvatthasyādhastānnyagrodhasya vāpāṃ vā samīpe vedyakṛtiṃ kṛtvā tasyāṃ catuṣkoṇavanaspatiśākhāyāmasaktacīrāyāṃ gandhasragdāmavatyāṃ caturdiśaṃ vinyastodakummasahiraṇyabījapiṭikāyāmapūpasrastaralājollopikamaṅgalaphalākṣavatyāṃ sarvagandhasarvarasasarvauṣadhīḥ sarvaratnāni copakalpya pratisaradadhimadhumodakasvastikanandyāvartavatyāmagniṃ praṇīyāśvatthapalāśakhadirarohitakodumbarāṇāmanyatamasyedhmamupasasādhāya tisraḥ pradhānadevatā yajatyuccaiḥśravasaṃ varuṇaṃ viṣṇumiti sthālīpākaiḥ paśubhiścāśvinau cāśvayujau cājyasya |
meaning: प्रागस्तमयान्निष्क्रम्योत्तरतो ग्रामस्य पुरस्ताद्वा शुचौ देशे ऽश्वत्थस्याधस्तान्न्यग्रोधस्य वापां वा समीपे वेद्यकृतिं कृत्वा तस्यां चतुष्कोणवनस्पतिशाखायामसक्तचीरायां गन्धस्रग्दामवत्यां चतुर्दिशं विन्यस्तोदकुम्मसहिरण्यबीजपिटिकायामपूपस्रस्तरलाजोल्लोपिकमङ्गलफलाक्षवत्यां सर्वगन्धसर्वरससर्वौषधीः सर्वरत्नानि चोपकल्प्य प्रतिसरदधिमधुमोदकस्वस्तिकनन्द्यावर्तवत्यामग्निं प्रणीयाश्वत्थपलाशखदिररोहितकोदुम्बराणामन्यतमस्येध्ममुपससाधाय तिस्रः प्रधानदेवता यजत्युच्चैःश्रवसं वरुणं विष्णुमिति स्थालीपाकैः पशुभिश्चाश्विनौ चाश्वयुजौ चाज्यस्य ।
text_mt:
Having gone out before sunset to the north or east of the village to a pure spot under an aśvattha or nyagrodha tree or near water, having made the shape of an altar, on which four-cornered branches of trees are placed, with bark attached, provided with garlands of fragrant wreaths, with water-jars and baskets of gold and seeds placed in the four directions, provided with cakes, layers of grass, parched grain, dumplings, auspicious fruits, and dice, and having prepared all perfumes, all saps, all herbs, and all jewels, provided with protective amulets, curds, honey, sweetmeats, svastika, and nandyāvarta figures, having brought forward the fire,

having arranged the firewood of any one among aśvattha, palāśa, khadira, rohitaka, or udumbara, he sacrifices to the three principal deities: to Uccaiḥśravas, Varuṇa, and Viṣṇu with pot-cooked offerings and animals, and to the two Aśvins and the two Āśvayujas with clarified butter.

sanskrit_iast: jayān hutvā yā oṣadhayaḥ samannyāyanti punantu mā pitaro 'gnermanva iti caturbhiranuvākaurapo 'bhimantryāśvānsnapayati |
meaning: जयान् हुत्वा या ओषधयः समन्न्यायन्ति पुनन्तु मा पितरो ऽग्नेर्मन्व इति चतुर्भिरनुवाकौरपो ऽभिमन्त्र्याश्वान्स्नपयति ।
text_mt: Having offered the Jaya offerings, having consecrated the water with the four sections: 'The plants which come together...', 'May the ancestors purify me...', and 'The follower of Agni...', he bathes the horses.
Having adorned them with wreaths and garlands of perfumes, they go clockwise thrice around the sacrificial place.
When the sacrifice is concluded, they go each to his place.
A cow and an ox are the sacrificial fee.

sanskrit_iast: āgrahāyaṇyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti apaḥ śvetapadāgrāhi pūrveṇa cāpareṇa ca | sapta ca vāruṇīrimāḥ prajāḥ sarvāśca rājabāndhavyaḥ svāhā || śveto ruṣatyo vidadhātyaśvo dadhadgarbhaṃ vṛṣaḥ satvaryāṃ jyok | samaṃ janāścakramayo vasānāḥ proṣādasāvirasi viśvametat || śetāya rauṣiśvāya svāhā na vai śvetasyābhyācāre ahirjaghāna kiṃcana | śvetāya vaitāhavyāya svāhā. || abhayaṃ naḥ prājāpatyebhyo bhūyāt svāhā || iti |
meaning: आग्रहायण्यां पौर्णमास्यां पयसि स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा तस्य जुहोति अपः श्वेतपदाग्राहि पूर्वेण चापरेण च । सप्त च वारुणीरिमाः प्रजाः सर्वाश्च राजबान्धव्यः स्वाहा ॥ श्वेतो रुषत्यो विदधात्यश्वो दधद्गर्भं वृषः सत्वर्यां ज्योक् । समं जनाश्चक्रमयो वसानाः प्रोषादसाविरसि विश्वमेतत् ॥ शेताय रौषिश्वाय स्वाहा न वै श्वेतस्याभ्याचारे अहिर्जघान किंचन । श्वेताय वैताहव्याय स्वाहा. ॥ अभयं नः प्राजापत्येभ्यो भूयात् स्वाहा ॥ इति ।

sanskrit_iast: srastare 'hataṃ vāsa udagdaśamāstīryodakāṃ vrīhīn yavānvāsya pariṣiñcati syonā pṛthivī bhaveti dvābhyāṃ sutrāmāṇamiti dvābhyām |
meaning: स्रस्तरे ऽहतं वास उदग्दशमास्तीर्योदकां व्रीहीन् यवान्वास्य परिषिञ्चति स्योना पृथिवी भवेति द्वाभ्यां सुत्रामाणमिति द्वाभ्याम् ।
text_mt: Having spread an unwashed garment with fringes to the north upon a bed of grass, he pours water around it, [or] rice, or barley, with the two verses: 'Be thou pleasant, O earth...' and the two verses: 'The good protector...'

sanskrit_iast: śamīśākhayā ca sapalāśayodañca triḥ samunmārṣṭi syonā pṛthivī bhaveti dvābhyāṃ sūtramāṇamiti dvābhyāṃ namo astu sarpebhya iti tisṛbhiśca |
meaning: शमीशाखया च सपलाशयोदञ्च त्रिः समुन्मार्ष्टि स्योना पृथिवी भवेति द्वाभ्यां सूत्रमाणमिति द्वाभ्यां नमो अस्तु सर्पेभ्य इति तिसृभिश्च ।
text_mt: And with a leafy branch of śamī, he sweeps thrice to the north with the two verses: 'Be thou pleasant, O earth...', the two verses: 'The good protector...', and the three verses: 'Homage to the serpents...'

sanskrit_iast: śāmyantu sarpāḥ svaśayā bhavantu ye antarikṣa uta ye divi śritāḥ | imāṃ mahīṃ pratyavarohema | śivāmajasrāṃ śivāṃ śāntāṃ suhemantāmuttarāmuttarāṃ samāṃkriyāsam || iti jyeṣṭha prathamānudīca āveśayati |
meaning: शाम्यन्तु सर्पाः स्वशया भवन्तु ये अन्तरिक्ष उत ये दिवि श्रिताः । इमां महीं प्रत्यवरोहेम । शिवामजस्रां शिवां शान्तां सुहेमन्तामुत्तरामुत्तरां समांक्रियासम् ॥ इति ज्येष्ठ प्रथमानुदीच आवेशयति ।
text_mt:
'May the serpents be appeased, may they rest peacefully, those that dwell in the mid-air and those in heaven!
May we descend upon this great earth;

May I make every successive year auspicious, unceasing, auspicious, peaceful, having a good winter!'—

saying this, he makes them lie down facing north, the eldest first.

sanskrit_iast: udīrghaṃ jīvo asurna āgādayaḥ prāgāttama ājyotireti | āraikapanthāṃ yātave sūryā-yāganmā yatna prataraṃ na āyuḥ | iti kaniṣṭhaprathamānujjihate |
meaning: उदीर्घं जीवो असुर्न आगादयः प्रागात्तम आज्योतिरेति । आरैकपन्थां यातवे सूर्या-यागन्मा यत्न प्रतरं न आयुः । इति कनिष्ठप्रथमानुज्जिहते ।

sanskrit_iast: na tatra stālīpāko na śākhayā samunmārṣṭi |
meaning: न तत्र स्तालीपाको न शाखया समुन्मार्ष्टि ।
text_mt: On that occasion there is no pot-cooked offering, nor does he sweep [the fire] with a branch.

sanskrit_iast: ayaṃ talpaḥ prataraṇo vasūnāṃ viśvārtvibhya ? talpo asmān | jyog jīvema sarvavīrā vayaṃ tama || iti talpamabhimantryate |
meaning: अयं तल्पः प्रतरणो वसूनां विश्वार्त्विभ्य ? तल्पो अस्मान् । ज्योग् जीवेम सर्ववीरा वयं तम ॥ इति तल्पमभिमन्त्र्यते ।
text_mt:
"This bed is a ferry to wealth […] bed to us; / may we live long, with all our men, [into old age]."

With these words he addresses the bed.
There are three central [full-moon days]: on the full moon day of Phālguna, of Āṣāḍha, and of Kārttika.
On these days there is a pot-cooked offering in milk; it has been explained.
After the full moon of Āgrahāyaṇa, before that of Phālguna, they are the eighth days of the dark fortnights.

sanskrit_iast: tāsu payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā tasya juhoti yā devyaṣṭakeṣvapasāpastamāstapā avayā asi | tvaṃ yajñe varuṇasyāvayā asi tasyai ta enā vidhema || ulūkhalā grāvāṇo ghoṣamakurvata haviḥ kṛṇvantaḥ parivatsarīyam ekāṣṭake suprajasaḥ suvīrā jyogjīvema balihṛdo vayaṃ te || yāṃ janāḥ pratinandanti rātrīṃ dhenumivāyatīm | saṃvatsarasya yā patnī sā no astu sumaṅgalī || saṃvatsarasya pratimāṃ ye tvā rātrīmupāsate | teṣāmāyuṣmatīṃ prajāṃrāyaspoṣeṇa saṃsṛjasva || iti catasraḥ sthālīpākasya |
meaning: तासु पयसि स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा तस्य जुहोति या देव्यष्टकेष्वपसापस्तमास्तपा अवया असि । त्वं यज्ञे वरुणस्यावया असि तस्यै त एना विधेम ॥ उलूखला ग्रावाणो घोषमकुर्वत हविः कृण्वन्तः परिवत्सरीयम् एकाष्टके सुप्रजसः सुवीरा ज्योग्जीवेम बलिहृदो वयं ते ॥ यां जनाः प्रतिनन्दन्ति रात्रीं धेनुमिवायतीम् । संवत्सरस्य या पत्नी सा नो अस्तु सुमङ्गली ॥ संवत्सरस्य प्रतिमां ये त्वा रात्रीमुपासते । तेषामायुष्मतीं प्रजांरायस्पोषेण संसृजस्व ॥ इति चतस्रः स्थालीपाकस्य ।
text_mt:
On these days, having cooked a pot-cooked offering in milk, he makes oblations of it:

"O goddess Aṣṭakā, who among active beings art the most active, a performer of penance, an expiator; / in the sacrifice thou art the expiation of Varuṇa; unto thee may we worship with these [oblations]."

"The mortars and the pressing-stones have made a sound, preparing the oblation of the full year;

O Ekāṣṭakā, rich in offspring, rich in heroes, bringing tribute to thee, may we live long."

"The night whom people welcome like a cow coming home, / she who is the consort of the year, may she be auspicious to us."

"They who worship thee, the night, as the image of the year: / unite their long-lived offspring with abundance of wealth."

These are the four [oblations] of the pot-cooked offering.

"To the Aṣṭakā possessing abundant gifts,

Svāhā!"—he appends [this] everywhere.

sanskrit_iast: hemanto vasante grīṣmaṛtavaḥ śivānaḥ śivāno varṣā abhayāściraṃ naḥ vaiśvānaro 'dhiratiḥ prāṇādo no ahorātre kṛṇutāṃ dīrghamāyuḥ || śāntā pṛthivī śivamantarikṣaṃ dyaur no devyabhayaṃ kṛṇotu | śivā diśaḥ pradiśa ādiśo na āpo vidyutaḥ paripāntvāyuḥ || āpo marīcīḥ paripāntu viśvato dhātā samudro abhayaṃ kṛṇotu | bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyaduta bhadramastu me brahmabhigūrttaṃ svarākṣāṇaḥ || kaviragnirindraḥ somaḥ sūryo vāyurastu me agnirvaiśvānaro apahantu pāpam | bṛhaspatiḥ savitā śarma yacchatu śriyaṃ virājaṃ mayi pūṣā dadhātu || iti pañacājyasya |
meaning: हेमन्तो वसन्ते ग्रीष्मऋतवः शिवानः शिवानो वर्षा अभयाश्चिरं नः वैश्वानरो ऽधिरतिः प्राणादो नो अहोरात्रे कृणुतां दीर्घमायुः ॥ शान्ता पृथिवी शिवमन्तरिक्षं द्यौर् नो देव्यभयं कृणोतु । शिवा दिशः प्रदिश आदिशो न आपो विद्युतः परिपान्त्वायुः ॥ आपो मरीचीः परिपान्तु विश्वतो धाता समुद्रो अभयं कृणोतु । भूतं भविष्यदुत भद्रमस्तु मे ब्रह्मभिगूर्त्तं स्वराक्षाणः ॥ कविरग्निरिन्द्रः सोमः सूर्यो वायुरस्तु मे अग्निर्वैश्वानरो अपहन्तु पापम् । बृहस्पतिः सविता शर्म यच्छतु श्रियं विराजं मयि पूषा दधातु ॥ इति पञचाज्यस्य ।
text_mt:
"May winter, spring, and summer, the seasons, be auspicious to us; may the rains be auspicious to us and free from danger for a long time; may Vaiśvānara, delight, and life-giver, may day and night make long life for us."

"May the earth be peaceful, the atmosphere auspicious; may the divine heaven bring us freedom from fear; / may the directions, intermediate directions, and quarters be auspicious to us; may waters and lightnings protect our life."

"May the waters and rays protect [us] from all sides; may Dhātṛ and the ocean make freedom from fear; / may what has been and what will be bring welfare to me; may the holy word, applauded, [bring] the light of heaven to us."

"May Agni the sage, Indra, Soma, Sūrya, and Vāyu be mine; may Agni Vaiśvānara strike away evil; / may Bṛhaspati and Savitṛ bestow protection; may Pūṣan place prosperity and sovereignty in me."
Having offered the Jaya oblations, with "The refreshment, O Agni!" [he offers to] Sviṣṭakṛt.

meaning: उत्तमायाः प्रदोषे चतुष्पथे ऽङ्गशो गां कारयेत् ।
text_mt: At dusk on the last [Aṣṭakā], at a crossroad, he should have a cow dismembered into parts.
Whosoever comes, to him he should give [a portion].

sanskrit_iast: tasyāvapāṃ juhuyāt vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitānvettha nihitānparāke medaso ghṛtasya kulyā abhiniḥsravantu satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā | iti |
meaning: तस्यावपां जुहुयात् वह वपां जातवेदः पितृभ्यो यत्रैतान्वेत्थ निहितान्पराके मेदसो घृतस्य कुल्या अभिनिःस्रवन्तु सत्याः सन्तु यजमानस्य कामाः स्वाहा । इति ।
text_mt: "Bear the omentum, O Jātavedas, to the ancestors, where thou knowest them deposited afar; let streams of fat and ghee flow forth; let the desires of the sacrificer be true, svāhā!"—thus.
Then with its breast he cooks boiled rice facing north.
The rest of it is explained by the ritual of the Aṣṭakā oblation.
He cooks the remaining portion.

meaning: श्वो ऽवशिष्टं भक्तं रन्धयित्वा पिण्डानामावृता त्रीन्मांसौदनपिण्डान्निदधाति ।
text_mt: On the next day, having cooked the remaining portion, according to the procedure for funerary balls he places three balls of boiled rice mixed with meat.
In the dark fortnight he should offer a śrāddha to the ancestors.
He should feed Brāhmaṇas with carefully prepared food; the Vedic revelation states: "One who does not know the Veda should not eat."

sanskrit_iast: yadi gavā paśunā vā kurvīta prokṣaṇamupapāyanaṃ paryagnikaraṇamulmukaharaṇaṃ vapāhomamiti |
meaning: यदि गवा पशुना वा कुर्वीत प्रोक्षणमुपपायनं पर्यग्निकरणमुल्मुकहरणं वपाहोममिति ।
text_mt: If he performs [it] with a cow or a victim, [there are]: the sprinkling, bringing forward, carrying of fire around, carrying of the firebrand, and the oblation of the omentum.
He should offer the omentum in three portions, as well as the pot-cooked offering and the cut-off portions.

sanskrit_iast: somāya pitṛmate svadhā nama iti juhoti yamāyāṅgirasvate pitṛmate svadhā nama iti dvitīyām | agnaye kāvyavāhanāya svadhā nama iti tṛtīyām |
meaning: सोमाय पितृमते स्वधा नम इति जुहोति यमायाङ्गिरस्वते पितृमते स्वधा नम इति द्वितीयाम् । अग्नये काव्यवाहनाय स्वधा नम इति तृतीयाम् ।
text_mt:
"To Soma accompanied by the ancestors, svadhā! homage!"—

with this he offers; "To Yama accompanied by the Aṅgirases and ancestors, svadhā! homage!" is the second; "To Agni, bearer of the oblations to ancestors, svadhā! homage!" is the third.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ māsi māsi niyataṃ tantraṃ piṇḍapitṛyajñe |
meaning: एवं मासि मासि नियतं तन्त्रं पिण्डपितृयज्ञे ।
text_mt: Thus month after month the procedure is fixed in the sacrifice of balls to the ancestors.

sanskrit_iast: phālgunyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ purastāddhānāpūpābhyāṃ bhagaṃ cāryamaṇaṃca yajet |
meaning: फाल्गुन्यां पौर्णमास्यां पुरस्ताद्धानापूपाभ्यां भगं चार्यमणंच यजेत् ।
text_mt: On the full moon day of Phālguna, beforehand, he should sacrifice to Bhaga and Aryaman with roasted barley and cakes.

sanskrit_iast: indrāṇyā haviṣyān piṣṭvā piṣṭāni samutpūya yāvanti paśujātāni tāvato mithunān pratirūpān śrapayitvā kāṃsye 'dhyājyānkṛtvā tenaiva rudrāya svāheti | īśānāyetyeke |
meaning: इन्द्राण्या हविष्यान् पिष्ट्वा पिष्टानि समुत्पूय यावन्ति पशुजातानि तावतो मिथुनान् प्रतिरूपान् श्रपयित्वा कांस्ये ऽध्याज्यान्कृत्वा तेनैव रुद्राय स्वाहेति । ईशानायेत्येके ।
text_mt: For Indrāṇī, having ground sacrificial grains and winnowed the meal, having cooked as many corresponding pairs as there are species of domestic animals, and having placed clarified butter on them in a bronze vessel, with that very [mixture he offers] with: "To Rudra, svāhā!"; "To Īśāna," according to some.
In the evening he proceeds with two cakes for Agni and Indra.

sanskrit_iast: āgneyastundilo na tasya striyaḥ prāśnanti sarvāmātyā itarasya |
meaning: आग्नेयस्तुन्दिलो न तस्य स्त्रियः प्राश्नन्ति सर्वामात्या इतरस्य ।
text_mt: The [cake] belonging to Agni is thick; women do not eat of it; all the family members [eat] of the other.
Or on the next day [he sacrifices] to Indrāṇī with a pot-cooked offering.

In sacrifices to groups [of deities], the sacrificial grass, the fire, the two foundation oblations, the two portions of clarified butter, the oblations of clarified butter, and the Sviṣṭakṛt are single.

sanskrit_iast: agnirindraḥ somaḥ sītā savitāsarasvatyaścinānumatī revatī rākā pūṣā rudra ityetairāyojana paryayana-pravapana-pralava-sītāyajña-khalayajñatantīyajñānaḍudyajñeṣvetā devatā iti yajati sāṃvatsareṣu ca parvasu |
meaning: अग्निरिन्द्रः सोमः सीता सवितासरस्वत्यश्चिनानुमती रेवती राका पूषा रुद्र इत्येतैरायोजन पर्ययन-प्रवपन-प्रलव-सीतायज्ञ-खलयज्ञतन्तीयज्ञानडुद्यज्ञेष्वेता देवता इति यजति सांवत्सरेषु च पर्वसु ।
text_mt: Agni, Indra, Soma, Sītā, Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, the two Aśvins, Anumati, Revatī, Rākā, Pūṣan, and Rudra: with these deities he sacrifices at the yoking, the ploughing around, the sowing, the harvesting, the furrow sacrifice, the threshing-floor sacrifice, the tethering-cord sacrifice, and the draft-ox sacrifice, and on the periodic days of the year.
At rivers, the ocean, wells, and tanks he sacrifices to Varuṇa; at herbs and trees to Soma; to Agni in the case of unspecified deities.
The building site should be level and rooted with plants.
Sloping to the south for one who desires food; [yet] offspring become subject to death there.
[Or] with water flowing together from all sides.
Or from which, after flowing together, the waters would drain to the northeast; that indeed [is suitable].

sanskrit_iast: gartaṃ khātvā yattaiḥ pāṃsubhiḥ pratipūryeta tadvā |
meaning: गर्तं खात्वा यत्तैः पांसुभिः प्रतिपूर्येत तद्वा ।
text_mt: Or where, having dug a pit, it would be refilled with that same earth; that indeed [is suitable].
If [the ground] is firm, it will be all the more watery.

sanskrit_iast: idamahaṃ viśamannādyāya tejase brahmavarcasāya parigṛhṇāmīti veśma parigṛhya garte hiraṇya nidhāyācyutāya dhruvāya bhaumāya svāheti juhoti |
meaning: इदमहं विशमन्नाद्याय तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसाय परिगृह्णामीति वेश्म परिगृह्य गर्ते हिरण्य निधायाच्युताय ध्रुवाय भौमाय स्वाहेति जुहोति ।
text_mt: Having enclosed the dwelling [site] with [the formula]: “Here I enclose the community for proper nourishment, for brilliance, for Vedic luster,” and having placed gold in the pit, he offers [clarified butter with]: “To Acyuta, to Dhruva, to Bhauma, svāhā!”
With the successive verses beginning with: “You are suitable,” he attends [to the site] in each direction, and with two in the middle.

sanskrit_iast: udakāṃsye 'śmānaṃ vrīhīnyavānvasya pariṣiñcati syonāpṛthivī bhaveti dvābhyāṃ sutramāṇāmiti dvābhyām |
meaning: उदकांस्ये ऽश्मानं व्रीहीन्यवान्वस्य परिषिञ्चति स्योनापृथिवी भवेति द्वाभ्यां सुत्रमाणामिति द्वाभ्याम् ।
text_mt:
Having placed a stone, rice, and barley into a bronze vessel of water, he sprinkles [the pit] around with the two [verses]: “Be pleasant, O earth,”

and with the two [verses beginning with]: “The well-protecting…”

sanskrit_iast: śamīśākhayā ca palāśayodañcaṃ triḥ samunmārṣṭi syonā prathivi bhaveti dvābhyāṃ sutramāṇamiti dvābhyāṃ namo astu sarpebhya iti tisṛbhiśca |
meaning: शमीशाखया च पलाशयोदञ्चं त्रिः समुन्मार्ष्टि स्योना प्रथिवि भवेति द्वाभ्यां सुत्रमाणमिति द्वाभ्यां नमो अस्तु सर्पेभ्य इति तिसृभिश्च ।
text_mt: With a twig of Śamī and with a Palāśa [leaf], he wipes [the pit] three times upward towards the north with the two [verses]: “Be pleasant, O earth,” with the two: “The well-protecting,” and with the three [verses]: “Homage be to the snakes.”

sanskrit_iast: idaṃ tat sarvato bhadramayamūrjo 'yaṃ rasaḥ | prāpyaivaṃ mānuṣānkāmānyadaśīrṣṇī tallapsyasi || iti madhyamāṃ sthūṇāmāsicya garta āsiñcati |
meaning: इदं तत् सर्वतो भद्रमयमूर्जो ऽयं रसः । प्राप्यैवं मानुषान्कामान्यदशीर्ष्णी तल्लप्स्यसि ॥ इति मध्यमां स्थूणामासिच्य गर्त आसिञ्चति ।
text_mt:
“This is all-propitious, this is vigor, this is sap; / having thus attained human desires, what you wished for, that you will obtain.”

Having poured [water] over the central post with this [verse], he pours it into the pit.

sanskrit_iast: ihaiva tiṣṭha nitarā tilvalā sthirāvati | madhye poṣasya puṣpatāmā tvā parisṛtaḥ kumbhaḥ | ā vatse jagato saha ā dadhnaḥ kalaśamairayam || iti madhyamāṃ sthūṇāmabhi mantryate |
meaning: इहैव तिष्ठ नितरा तिल्वला स्थिरावति । मध्ये पोषस्य पुष्पतामा त्वा परिसृतः कुम्भः । आ वत्से जगतो सह आ दध्नः कलशमैरयम् ॥ इति मध्यमां स्थूणामभि मन्त्र्यते ।
text_mt:
“Stand firmly right here, fertile, endowed with stability; / flourishing in the midst of abundance, may the jar poured around come to you!

Together with the calf of the living world, I have brought forth a jar of curds.”

With these [verses], he addresses the central post.
With [the formula]: “You are of the Vasus, of the vigor of the Vasus, and of the day and night,” he erects the post in the pit.

sanskrit_iast: ṛte 'vasthūṇā adhiroha vaṃśo agne virājamupasedhaśakram || iti madhyamaṃ vaṃ śamavadadāti |
meaning: ऋते ऽवस्थूणा अधिरोह वंशो अग्ने विराजमुपसेधशक्रम् ॥ इति मध्यमं वं शमवददाति ।
text_mt:
“According to cosmic order, mount the posts, O cross-beam! O fire, drive away the radiant Indra!”

With this [verse], he lays down the central cross-beam.
The remaining posts and beams [are erected] silently.

sanskrit_iast: prāgdvāraṃ dakṣiṇādvāraṃ vā māpayitvā gṛhānahaṃ sumanasaḥ prapadye vīraṃ hītyetayā prapadyate yathā purastādvyākhyātam |

text_mt: Having measured out [a house] with an eastward entrance or a southward entrance, he enters [it] with [the verse]: “With a cheerful mind, I enter the house…” as has been explained before.

sanskrit_iast: praiturājā varuṇo revatībhirasminsthāne tiṣṭhatu puṣyamāṇaḥ | irāṃ vahantī ghṛtamukṣamāṇāsteṣvahaṃ sumanāḥ saṃ vasāma || ityuttarapūrvasyāṃ diśi pratipānamudakumbhamavasthāpayati |
meaning: प्रैतुराजा वरुणो रेवतीभिरस्मिन्स्थाने तिष्ठतु पुष्यमाणः । इरां वहन्ती घृतमुक्षमाणास्तेष्वहं सुमनाः सं वसाम ॥ इत्युत्तरपूर्वस्यां दिशि प्रतिपानमुदकुम्भमवस्थापयति ।
text_mt:
“May King Varuṇa go forth with the wealthy [waters]; may he remain in this place, thriving.

Bringing refreshing food, sprinkling clarified butter—among them may I, cheerful-minded, dwell.”

With these [verses], he sets down a water-jar for drinking in the northeast direction.

sanskrit_iast: samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomi svāṃyonimabhigacchata ariṣṭā asmākaṃ vīrā mā parāseci matpayaḥ | ityudañcanam |
meaning: समुद्रं वः प्रहिणोमि स्वांयोनिमभिगच्छत अरिष्टा अस्माकं वीरा मा परासेचि मत्पयः । इत्युदञ्चनम् ।
text_mt: “I send you to the ocean; go to your own source! / May our men be uninjured; may my milk not be poured away!” / — [with this verse he sets down] the water-dipper.

meaning: वास्तोष्पत्यं पयसि स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा तस्य जुहोति । अमीवहा वास्तोष्पते वास्तोष्पत इत्येताभ्याम् वास्तोष्पते प्रतरणो न अधि गयस्फानो गोभिरश्वेभिरिन्दो अजरासस्ते सख्ये व्याम पितेव पुत्रान्प्रति नो जुषस्व ॥ वास्तोष्पते शग्मया सं सदा ते सक्षीमहि रणवया गातुमत्या पाहि क्षेम उत योगे वरं नो यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा नः ॥ इति ।
text_mt:
Having cooked a pot-cooked offering to Vāstoṣpati in milk, he makes an oblation of it with these two [verses beginning with]: “O Vāstoṣpati, destroyer of disease…” and “O Vāstoṣpati…”:

“O Vāstoṣpati, being an increaser over us, increasing our possessions with cattle and horses, O drop! / May we abide unaging in your friendship; welcome us as a father does his sons!

O Vāstoṣpati, through your delightful, blissful companionship may we be united; protect our welfare in peaceful possession and in enterprise! Do you always protect us with blessings!”
From [the food] prepared for the All-gods, he should offer the Bali oblation in the evening and in the morning.

sanskrit_iast: agnīṣomau dhanvantariṃ viśvāndevānprajāpatimagniṃ sviṣṭakṛtamityevaṃ homo vidhīyate |

text_mt: The oblation is prescribed thus: to Agni and Soma, to Dhanvantari, to the All-gods, to Prajāpati, and to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt.

sanskrit_iast: atha baliṃ haratyagnaye namaḥ somāya dhanvantaraye viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ prajāpataye agnaye sviṣṭakṛta ityagnyāgāra uttarāmuttarām |

text_mt: Then he offers the Bali: “Homage to Agni, to Soma, to Dhanvantari, to the All-gods, to Prajāpati, to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt,” in the fire-house, each further to the north.
“To the waters,” near the water-jar.

text_mt: “To the herbs, to the trees,” at the central post of the house.
“To the domestic deities,” in the middle of the house.
“To Dharma, to Adharma,” at the door.
“To Death, to Space,” in the open space.
“To the inside of the cowpen,” inside the cowpen.
“To the outer Vaiśravaṇa,” outside towards the east.
“To the All-gods,” in the dwelling.
“To Indra and Indra’s men,” in the east.
“To Yama and Yama’s men,” in the south.
“To Varuṇa and Varuṇa’s men,” in the west.
“To Soma and Soma’s men,” in the north.
“To Brahmā and Brahmā’s men,” in the middle.

text_mt: Having mixed [the remaining food] with water, he should pour out the remainder to the south on the ground with: “To the ancestors, svadhā!”
Having washed his hands and sipped water, having fed the guest, he should eat of what remains.
Now, therefore, we shall explain the rite of Ṣaṣṭhī.
On the fifth day of the bright fortnight, facing west, he should eat sacrificial food.

text_mt: He should sleep on the ground on Darbha grass or rice straw, with his head towards the east, observing celibacy.

text_mt: On the next day, after the sun has risen, he should not refuse a bath, drink, food, ointment, garlands, or garments.
He should eat as much as [the host] gives, and he should eat whatever [the host] gives, except from impure persons or sinners, excluding stale food.

sanskrit_iast: astamita āditye payasi sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvāthaitairnāmadheyairjuhoti dhanadāṃ vasumīśānāṃ kāmadāṃ sarvakāminām puṇyāṃ yaśasvinīṃ devīṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ śakra juṣasva me || nandī bhūtiśca lakṣmīścādityā ca yaśasvinī sumanā vāk ca siddhiśca ṣaṣṭhī me diśatāṃ dhanam || putrānpaśūndhanaṃ dhānyaṃ bahvaścājagaveḍakam manasā yatpraṇītaṃ ca tanme diśatu havyabhuk || kānadāṃ rajanīṃ viśvarūpāṃ ṣaṣṭhīmupavarttatu me dhanam sāma kāma kāmapatnī ṣaṣṭhī me diśatāṃ dhanam || ākṛtiḥ prakṛtivarcanī dhāvaniḥ padmacāriṇī manmanā bhava svāhā || gandhadvārāṃ durādharṣāṃ nityapuṣṭāṃ karīṣiṇīm īśvarīṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tāmihopahvaye śriyam | nānāpatrakā ka sā devī puṣṭiścātisarasvatī ariṃ devīṃ prapadyeyamupavarttayatu me dhanam || hiraṇyaprakārādevi māṃ vara āgacchatvāyuryaśaśca svāhā || aśvapūrṇāṃ rathamadhyāṃ hastinādapramodinīm | śriyaṃ devīmupavhaye śrīrmādevī juṣatām || upayantu māṃ devagaṇāstyā nā gāśca tapasā saha | prādurbhūto 'smi rāṣṭre 'smin śrīḥ śraddhāṃ kīrtiṃ vṛddhiṃ ga. ca. dadhātu me || śriyai svāhā hriyai svāhā lakṣmyai svāhā upalakṣmyai svāhā nanhāyai svāhā haridrāyai svāhā ṣaṣṭhyai svāhā samṛddhyai svāhā jayāyai svāhā kāmāyai svāheti |
meaning: अस्तमित आदित्ये पयसि स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वाथैतैर्नामधेयैर्जुहोति धनदां वसुमीशानां कामदां सर्वकामिनाम् पुण्यां यशस्विनीं देवीं षष्ठीं शक्र जुषस्व मे ॥ नन्दी भूतिश्च लक्ष्मीश्चादित्या च यशस्विनी सुमना वाक् च सिद्धिश्च षष्ठी मे दिशतां धनम् ॥ पुत्रान्पशून्धनं धान्यं बह्वश्चाजगवेडकम् मनसा यत्प्रणीतं च तन्मे दिशतु हव्यभुक् ॥ कानदां रजनीं विश्वरूपां षष्ठीमुपवर्त्ततु मे धनम् साम काम कामपत्नी षष्ठी मे दिशतां धनम् ॥ आकृतिः प्रकृतिवर्चनी धावनिः पद्मचारिणी मन्मना भव स्वाहा ॥ गन्धद्वारां दुराधर्षां नित्यपुष्टां करीषिणीम् ईश्वरीं सर्वभूतानां तामिहोपह्वये श्रियम् । नानापत्रका क सा देवी पुष्टिश्चातिसरस्वती अरिं देवीं प्रपद्येयमुपवर्त्तयतु मे धनम् ॥ हिरण्यप्रकारादेवि मां वर आगच्छत्वायुर्यशश्च स्वाहा ॥ अश्वपूर्णां रथमध्यां हस्तिनादप्रमोदिनीम् । श्रियं देवीमुपव्हये श्रीर्मादेवी जुषताम् ॥ उपयन्तु मां देवगणास्त्या ना गाश्च तपसा सह । प्रादुर्भूतो ऽस्मि राष्ट्रे ऽस्मिन् श्रीः श्रद्धां कीर्तिं वृद्धिं ग. च. दधातु मे ॥ श्रियै स्वाहा ह्रियै स्वाहा लक्ष्म्यै स्वाहा उपलक्ष्म्यै स्वाहा नन्हायै स्वाहा हरिद्रायै स्वाहा षष्ठ्यै स्वाहा समृद्ध्यै स्वाहा जयायै स्वाहा कामायै स्वाहेति ।
text_mt:
When the sun has set, having cooked a pot-cooked offering in milk, he then offers oblations with these names: / “The giver of wealth, the ruler of treasure, the granter of desires to all who have desires, / the auspicious, renowned goddess Ṣaṣṭhī—O powerful one, be pleased with my [offering]!

Nandī, and Bhūti, and Lakṣmī, and Ādityā the renowned, / Sumanā, Vāc, and Siddhi: may Ṣaṣṭhī bestow wealth upon me!”

Sons, cattle, wealth, grain, many horses, goats, and sheep, / and whatever is brought forth by the mind—may the oblation-eater bestow that on me!

Granting desires, the night, multiform, may wealth come to me [through] Ṣaṣṭhī! / Sāman, desire, the wife of desire—may Ṣaṣṭhī bestow wealth on me!

Form, shining origin, flowing, moving on a lotus, be inclined toward me, svāhā!

Approachable through fragrance, unassailable, ever thriving, rich in dung, / the ruler of all beings—her, Śrī, do I invoke here.

That goddess possessing various leaves, and nourishment, exceeding Sarasvatī— / may I approach the foe-subduing goddess; may she cause wealth to turn toward me!

O goddess of golden forms, may the best boon come to me, life and fame, svāhā!

Rich in horses, amidst chariots, rejoicing in the roar of elephants, / I invoke the goddess Śrī; may the goddess Śrī take pleasure in me!

May the troops of gods and the serpent-demons approach me along with austerity; / I have become manifest in this realm; may Śrī grant me faith, fame, prosperity, and [...]!

To Śrī, svāhā; to Hrī, svāhā; to Lakṣmī, svāhā; to Upalakṣmī, svāhā; to Nanhā, svāhā; to Haridrā, svāhā; to Ṣaṣṭhī, svāhā; to Samṛddhi, svāhā; to Jayā, svāhā; to Kāmā, svāhā.
He should employ [this ritual] for six months, or three fortnights on each side.
An application of a hundred thousand [oblations], or [it may be done] as a single boon.
A cow and a draft-ox are the sacrificial fee.
Now then we shall explain the Vināyakas.
Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa, Kūṣmāṇḍarājaputra, Usmita, and Devayajana.
These are the symptoms of those possessed by them:
He sees men clad in reddish garments.
He sees camels, pigs, donkeys, outcasts, and other impure dreams.
Walking along a road, he thinks, "Someone is following behind me."

text_mt: Possessed indeed by these Vināyakas, princes possessing auspicious marks do not obtain kingship.
Maidens desiring a husband, possessing auspicious marks, do not obtain husbands.

meaning: स्त्रियः प्रजाकामा लक्षणवत्यः प्रजां न लभन्ते ।
text_mt: Women desiring offspring, possessing auspicious marks, do not obtain offspring.
The children of virtuous women die.
For merchants, trade fails.
For farmers, agriculture yields little fruit.
Soil from an anthill, earth from a crab-hole, yellow pigment, and bdellium.
From four springs he should fetch four unbroken water-jars.
Having prepared all perfumes, all saps, all herbs, all jewels, an amulet-cord, curds, honey, and clarified butter,

meaning: एतान् संभारान्संसृज्य ऋषभचर्मारुह्याथैनं सहस्राक्षं शतधारमृषिभिः पावनं कृतम् । ताभिष्ट्वाभिषिञ्चामि पावमानीः पुनन्तु त्वा ॥ अग्निना दत्ता इन्द्रेण दत्ता सोमेन दत्ता वरुणेन दत्ता वायुना दत्ता,विष्णुना दत्ता बृहस्पतिना दत्ता विश्वैर्देवैर्दत्तः सर्वैर्देवैर्दत्ता ओषधय आपो वरुणसंमितास्ताभिष्ट्वाभिषिञ्चामि पावमानीः पुनन्तु त्वेति सर्वत्रानुषजति यत्ते केशेषु दैर्भाग्यं सीमन्ते तत्र मूर्द्धनि । ललाटे कर्णयोरक्ष्णोरापस्त तु ते सदा ॥ भगं ते वरुणे राजा भ्र सूर्यो बृहस्पतिः । भगमिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च सप्तर्षयो ददुः ॥ इति ।

having mixed these materials, having mounted a bull's hide, then [he sprinkles] him [with the verse]:

"Thousand-eyed, flowing in a hundred streams, made purifying by the seers— / with these I sprinkle you; may the purifying [waters] cleanse you!"

"Given by Agni, given by Indra, given by Soma, given by Varuṇa, given by Vāyu, given by Viṣṇu, given by Bṛhaspati, given by the Viśvedevas, given by all the gods—the herbs, the waters measured by Varuṇa—with these I sprinkle you; may the purifying [waters] cleanse you!"

on the forehead, in the ears, in the eyes—may the waters [remove] for you always!

Good fortune for you king Varuṇa, [...] the Sun, Bṛhaspati,

At [...] night, with mustard oil pressed on the same day, using an udumbara ladle, he offers four oblations: "To Śālakaṭaṅkaṭa, svāhā; to Kūṣmāṇḍarājaputra, svāhā; to Usmita, svāhā; to Devayajana, svāhā."

sanskrit_iast: ata ūrdhvaṃ grāmacatuṣpathe nagaracatuṣpathe nigamacatuṣpathe sarvatomukhāndarbhānāstīrya nave śūrpe balimupaharati phalīkṛtāṃstaṇḍulānaphalīkṛtāṃstaṇḍulānāmaṃ māṃsaṃ pakvaṃ māṃsamāmānmatsyānpakvānmatsyān āmānapūpānpakvānapūpānpiṣṭāngandhānapiṣṭāngandhā madhupānaṃ maireyapānaṃ surāpānaṃ muktaṃ mālyaṃ grathithaṃ mālyaṃ raktaṃ mālyaṃ śuklaṃ mālyaṃ raktapītaśuklakṛṣṇanīlaharitacitravāsāṃsi mākalmāṣamūlabhalamiti |

text_mt: Thereafter, at a village crossroads, a town crossroads, or a market crossroads, having strewn darbha grass pointing in all directions, he presents an offering in a new winnowing-basket: husked rice grains, unhusked rice grains, raw meat, cooked meat, raw fish, cooked fish, raw cakes, cooked cakes, ground scents, unground scents, [...] mead-drink, maireya-drink, liquor-drink, loose garlands, strung garlands, red garlands, white garlands, red, yellow, white, black, blue, green, and multi-colored garments, and variegated roots and fruits.

sanskrit_iast: atha devānāmāvāhanaṃ vimukhaḥ śeyeno bako yakṣaḥ kalaho bhīrurvināyakaḥ kūṣmāṇḍarā yajñāvikṣepī kulaṅgāpamāro yūpakeśī sūparakroḍī haimavato jambhako virūpākṣo lohitākṣo vaiśravaṇo mahāseno mahādevo mahārāja iti | ete me devāḥ prīyantāṃ prītā māṃ prīṇayantu tṛptā māṃ tarpayantviti |
meaning: अथ देवानामावाहनं विमुखः शेयेनो बको यक्षः कलहो भीरुर्विनायकः कूष्माण्डरा यज्ञाविक्षेपी कुलङ्गापमारो यूपकेशी सूपरक्रोडी हैमवतो जम्भको विरूपाक्षो लोहिताक्षो वैश्रवणो महासेनो महादेवो महाराज इति । एते मे देवाः प्रीयन्तां प्रीता मां प्रीणयन्तु तृप्ता मां तर्पयन्त्विति ।
text_mt: Then the invocation of the gods: "Vimukha, Śyena, Baka, Yakṣa, Kalaha, Bhīru, Vināyaka, Kūṣmāṇḍarā[japutra], Yajñāvikṣepin, Kulaṅgāpamāra, Yūpakeśin, Sūparakroḍin, Haimavata, Jambhaka, Virūpākṣa, Lohitākṣa, Vaiśravaṇa, Mahāsena, Mahādeva, Mahārāja! / May these gods be pleased with me; being pleased, may they satisfy me; being satisfied, may they refresh me!"

sanskrit_iast: adhiṣṭhiter'ddharātra ācāryo grahānupatiṣṭhate | bhagavati bhagaṃ me dedi varṇavati varṇaṃ me dehi rūpavati rūpaṃ me dehi tejasvini tejo me dehi yaśasvini yaśo me dehi putravati putrānme dehi sarvavati sarvānkāmānme pradehīti |
